verdict.rationale: Daytona has its own published OpenAPI spec, official Python/TypeScript SDKs, and a CLI for programmatically managing sandbox lifecycle, snapshots, code execution, computer use, and more, so its core surface is API-accessible. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly states or verifies that the API matches the UI feature-for-feature. missing for 10: an explicit documented API/UI parity statement, evidence that dashboard-only features (e.g., the web terminal, account or org settings) have API equivalents, independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Sandboxes are isolated runtime environments you can manage programmatically to run code.
Daytona provides command-line access to core features for interacting with Daytona Sandboxes, including managing their lifecycle, snapshots, and more.
Includes references and practical patterns for the Daytona API, CLI, Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby SDKs.
Computer Use enables programmatic control of desktop environments within sandboxes.
